title: Grateful Dead Live at The Silver Dollar Fair on 1968-11-01
lineage: SBD > MR > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with a great Jerry‑forward mix but plagued by mid‑show dropouts; still delivers a monster The Other One and stellar Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The performance shines despite serious tape problems – reviewers rave about the fiery Dark Star, crushing The Other One (especially the Cryptical > TOO segment), and the sweet Feedback. The soundboard mix puts Jerry’s guitar front‑and‑center, letting his analog feedback sing, but the audio collapses after New Potato, leaving large unlistenable gaps. Overall the music outweighs the technical flaws for dedicated listeners.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is consistently praised as exceptional (many 4‑5 star comments) while recording quality is described as severely degraded in the middle; weighted average yields a solid 4‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Excellent Jerry‑forward mix for guitar feedback, but the tape deteriorates after the New Potato/cryptical envelopment section. Dropouts and muffled audio make a large middle portion unlistenable; later sections recover somewhat.

show_quality.setlist_flow: One‑set show that opens with a powerful Dark Star, moves through intense jams (New Potato, Cryptical Envelopment) before the recording collapses, then resurfaces with a ferocious The Other One and finishes strong with Caution → Feedback → Good Night.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his soaring guitar tone, foreground placement in the mix, and blistering solos on The Other One; occasional burial later but still brilliant.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for off‑the‑charts interplay with Garcia during The Other One, highlighting bass brilliance.
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned only briefly – some feel his guitar gets buried in the latter mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Long drum solo described as uninteresting; overall percussion not a focus of praise.
